Rashi on Shabbat 127b:12:1.english: A royal matter - And it is necessary to conceal it.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:13:1.hebrew: צינורא - רוק. וגזרו על הנכרים שיהיו כזבים לכל דבריהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 127b:13:1.english: Tzinora - Spittle. And [the Sages] decreed regarding gentiles that they are like zavim in all respects.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:15:1.hebrew: מאכילין לעניים דמאי - לא אסרוהו עליהם, מפני שצריכים לחזר על פתח ע"ה, וסמכו על שרוב עמי הארץ מעשרין:
Rashi on Shabbat 127b:15:1.english: One [may] feed the poor demai - [The Sages] did not forbid it to them because they need to go around to the door of an am ha'aretz [an unlearned person], and [the Sages] relied on [the fact] that the majority of amei ha'aretz tithe.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:15:2.hebrew: אכסניא - חיל של מלך ישראל, ומטילו על בני העיר לפרנסן:
Rashi on Shabbat 127b:15:2.english: Soldiers [akhsanya] - An army of a Jewish king, which he imposes upon the townspeople to sustain them.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:16:1.hebrew: שניטלה תרומתו - קס"ד תרומת מעשר שהלוי נותן לכהן, וכ"ש תרומה גדולה שיש על ישראל להפריש, והפרישו קודם שנתן המעשר ללוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 127b:16:1.english: Whose terumah has been taken - We initially assumed [that this refers to] terumat ma'aser [the terumah of the tithe], which the Levite gives to the priest, and all the more so terumah gedolah [the great terumah], which an Israelite is obligated to separate and [already] separated before giving the tithe to the Levite.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:17:1.hebrew: שהקדימו בשבולין - לתרומה. ישראל היה לו להפריש תרומה גדולה תחילה, דכתיב (שמוח כב) מלאתך ודמעך לא תאחר: מלאתך אלו בכורים — מכאן שהמקדים תרומה לבכורים לוקה; ודמעך זו תרומה — שאם הקדים מעשר לתרומה לוקה. והנ"מ משנתמרח בכרי, לוקה אם הקדים מעשר לתרומה; אבל הקדים למעשר קודם לתרומה בשבלים, אינו לוקה:
Rashi on Shabbat 127b:17:1.english: In a case in which he preceded it on the stalks - [i.e., preceded] terumah. An Israelite should have separated terumah gedolah first, as it is written (Exodus 22[:28]), "You shall not delay your fullness and your outflow": "your fullness" — this refers to bikkurim [first fruits], from here [we derive] that one who separates terumah before bikkurim receives lashes; and "your outflow" — this refers to terumah, [meaning] that if one separated ma'aser [tithe] before terumah, he receives lashes. And this applies only once [the grain] has been smoothed in a pile — he receives lashes if he separated ma'aser before terumah; however, [if] he separated ma'aser before terumah [while it was still] on the stalks, he does not receive lashes.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:17:2.english: And you shall set apart from it - [This] is written regarding the Levites, concerning the teruma of the tithe.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:18:1.hebrew: מכל מתנותיכם וגו' - נמי בלוים כתיב גבי תרומת מעשר, וקאמר: "את כל תרומת ה'". "כל" — משמע כל צד תרומה שבו:
Rashi on Shabbat 127b:18:1.english: From all your gifts, etc. - [This] is also written regarding the Levites, concerning terumat ma'aser, and it states: "all the teruma of the Lord." "All" implies every aspect of teruma in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:19:1.english: This - [the grain] that was smoothed [into a pile].

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:19:2.hebrew: אידגן - וחלה עליו חובת תרומה, כדכתיב (דברים י״ח:ד׳) "ראשית דגנך". הלכך, כי שקלה לוי, בעי אהדורי לכהן תרי ממאה שבו ברישא, והדר אחד מעשרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 127b:19:2.english: Have become grain - And the obligation of terumah has taken effect upon it, as it is written (Deuteronomy 18:4): “The first of your grain.” Therefore, when a Levite takes it [as first tithe], he must return to the priest two out of a hundred of it first [as terumah gedolah], and then one out of ten [as terumat ma'aser].

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג הני נמי בהני שייכי - הכנסת אורחים וביקור חולים היינו גמילות חסדים, ועיון תפלה היינו בכלל גמילות חסדים, דכתיב (משלי י״א:י״ז) "גומל נפשו איש חסד". השכמת בית המדרש וגידול בנים לתלמוד תורה היינו תלמוד תורה. דן את חבירו לכף זכות בכלל הבאת שלום, דמתוך שהוא מכריעו לזכות ואמר "לא חטא לי בזאת, אנוס היה או לטובה נתכוון", יש שלום ביניהן. ורבי יוחנן לפרש לך אתא, דבכלל ג' דמתניתין איתנהו להנך ו', ואיכא נמי לכבוד אב ואם, ורבי יוחנן לא פליג עליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 127b:1:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: These too are attributable to those - Hospitality toward guests and visiting the sick are acts of loving-kindness, and devotion in prayer is included in acts of loving-kindness, as it is written (Proverbs 11:17): "A kind man does good to his own soul." Attending the study hall early and raising children for Torah study are [forms of] Torah study. Judging one's fellow favorably is included in bringing peace, for since he tips the scale in his favor and says, "He did not sin against me in this; he was forced by circumstances or intended it for good," there is peace between them. And Rabbi Yochanan came to explain to you that those six [items] are included in the three [items] of our Mishnah, and there is also honoring father and mother, and Rabbi Yochanan does not disagree with it.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:21:1.english: That it is bitter - [Meaning] that it is bitter.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:2:1.english: In anguish - With sorrow of soul.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:4:1.english: Leased - [Meaning] that he gives it to another for such-and-such [a number of] kor per year.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:6:1.hebrew: כל היכא דאמרינן מעשה בחסיד אחד, או רבי יהודה בן בבא או רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 127b:6:1.english: Wherever we say "an incident involving a certain pious man," [it refers to] either Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava or Rabbi Yehudah bar Rabbi Ilai.

Rashi on Shabbat 127b:7:1.english: Who is not proven to the rabbi - That [the rabbi] does not know his character traits [enough] to rely on him and leave her with us.

Tosafot on Shabbat 127b:14:1.hebrew: כיון דחזיא לכהן שפיר דמי - אע"ג דאמר בשילהי כירה (לעיל שבת דף מז.) דבגדי עניים לעשירים לא, הכא לכ"ע חזיא, אלא איסורא הוא דרביע עליה; אבל התם לא חזו מחמת גריעותא. ומהאי טעמא נמי לא אמרינן התם טעמא דבסמוך, דאי בעי מפקר לנכסיה. והא דאמר בפרק כל הכלים (לעיל שבת ד' קכה.): "שירי פרוזמיות שאין בהן ג' על ג' אין מטלטלין אותן", משמע הא יש בהן שלש על שלש מטלטלים — היינו לעניים, א"נ אפילו לעשירים בבית עניים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 127b:14:1.english: Since it is suitable for a priest, one may well [move it] - Although [the Gemara] states at the end of [the chapter] Keirah (above, Shabbat 47a) that garments of the poor are not [permitted to be moved] by the rich, here [in the case of terumah] it is fit for everyone, except that a prohibition rests upon it; but there [with garments of the poor], they are not fit [for the rich] due to [their] inferiority. And for this same reason, we also do not state there the reason [given] immediately below: "that if he wishes, he can renounce ownership of his property." And [as for] that which [the Gemara] states in the chapter Kol HaKelim (above, Shabbat 125a): "Remnants of cloaks [perozemiyyot] that do not measure three by three [fingerbreadths] may not be moved" — which implies that if they do measure three by three, they may be moved — that refers to the poor, or alternatively, even to the rich in a poor person's house.

Tosafot on Shabbat 127b:15:1.hebrew: דאי בעי מפקר לנכסיה - הוה מצי למימר כדלעיל, כיון דחזי לעניים; אלא כיון דמשכח טעמא דאפי' לדידיה מצי חזי — אמר. ובפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף לה:) ובפרק שלשה שאכלו (ברכות ד' מז.) איצטריך להאי טעמא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 127b:15:1.english: For if he desires, he may renounce his property - [The Gemara] could have said as above, "Since it is suitable [for the poor]"; however, since it found a reason whereby it can even be suitable for him [himself], it stated [that reason]. And in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 35b) and in the chapter [entitled] Sheloshah She'akhlu (Berakhot 47a), this reason is needed.

Tosafot on Shabbat 127b:19:1.hebrew: האי אידגן - מדנקט אידגן, משמע אפי' לא ראה פני הבית. תימה: אכתי אפילו הקדימו בכרי נמי לא לחייב אלא באידגן וראה פני הבית? וי"ל: דאי לא כתב "והרמותם", ה"א דכולם חייבין אפילו לא אידגן; השתא דכתי' קרא, מוקמי ליה במסתבר, דהיינו לא אידגן, שאפילו ראה פני הבית לא היה חייב. א"נ י"ל: הא דנקט אידגן — היינו ככל דינו, שראה פני הבית, אלא דמילתא דפסיקא נקט, דאיכא למאן דאמר בבא מציעא (דף פח:) דלא בעינן ראיית פני הבית אלא בזיתים וענבים, דלאו בני גורן נינהו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 127b:19:1.english: This has become grain - Since [Abaye] used the term "it has become grain," it implies [that it is obligated in teruma gedola] even if it has not seen the front of the house [i.e., been brought into the house]. [This is] surprising: still, even if [the Levite] anticipated [and separated first tithe] in the pile, should it not also be obligated only when it has become grain and seen the front of the house? And one can answer that if [the verse] had not written "and you shall set apart" (vaharemotem), I would have thought that all of them are obligated even if it had not become grain; now that the verse is written, we apply it to the reasonable case — namely, [where] it has not become grain, for even if it had seen the front of the house it would not have been obligated. Alternatively, one can answer that [when Abaye] stated "it has become grain," it means according to its full law — that it saw the front of the house; rather, he stated a categorical rule, because there is an opinion in Bava Metzia (88b) that we do not require seeing the front of the house except for olives and grapes, which are not subject to the threshing floor.

Tosafot on Shabbat 127b:20:1.hebrew: הא קמ"ל דאין חומש מעכב - ואף על גב דמבעיא לן בפרק הזהב (בבא מציעא דף נד.) אי מעכב אי לא, ולא פשיט מהכא — משום דהוה מצי למידחי דאגב אחרינא תנייה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 127b:20:1.english: This teaches us that the fifth does not invalidate [the redemption] - Even though we raise a dilemma in the chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 54a) whether it invalidates [the redemption] or not, and [the Gemara there] does not resolve [it] from here — [that is] because one could deflect [the proof by arguing] that [the Mishnah] taught it incidentally along with another [case].
